items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ on Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dt\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and spatial orientation $\epsilon_{123}=1$. Fix the global gauge group $SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$, and the trivial right principal $SU(2)$-bundle over each spatial slice. Let

$$T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a\quad(a=1,2,3),\qquad \kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY),$$

where $\sigma_a$ are the Pauli matrices and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ has basis $T_1,T_2,T_3$. Thus $[T_a,T_b]=\epsilon_{abc}T_c$ and $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g$ is dimensionless. The scalar field is one real adjoint Higgs field: a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued map $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^3$, viewed as the real form in the complexified adjoint representation. A gauge connection is a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form $A=A_i dx^i$. In a local section change $s_j=s_i h_{ij}$, use the right-action convention $A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+h_{ij}^{-1}dh_{ij}$ and $\Phi_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}\Phi_i$. Define

$$F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j],\qquad D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi],\qquad B_i=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}.$$

The static spacetime fields are the smooth maps $\widetilde\Phi,\widetilde A_\mu:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathfrak{su}(2)$, $\mu=0,1,2,3$, defined by $\widetilde\Phi(t,x)=\Phi(x)$, $\widetilde A_i(t,x)=A_i(x)$, and $\widetilde A_0(t,x)=0$; thus $\partial_t\widetilde A_i=\partial_t\widetilde\Phi=0$. The spacetime connection is $\widetilde A=\widetilde A_\mu dx^\mu$, with $x^0=t$. This Prasad–Sommerfield sector has no other dynamical fields and identically zero Higgs potential. Its adopted energy functional is

$$E[A,\Phi]=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x.$$

The field dimensions are $[A_i]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and $[F_{ij}]=[B_i]=[D_i\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, so $E$ has dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$. A configuration is finite-energy when this integral is finite.

The boundary data fix $v>0$ of dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and require $\Phi(R\,\cdot)/v\to n_\infty$ in $C^\infty(S^2,\mathfrak{su}(2))$, where $S^2=\{\omega\in\mathbb R^3:|\omega|=1\}$ has its outward orientation and $|n_\infty|_\kappa=1$; here $|X|_\kappa^2:=\kappa(X,X)$. In particular $|\Phi(R\omega)|_\kappa\to v$ uniformly. The stabilizer subgroup of $T_3$ is $U(1)=\{\exp(\theta T_3):\theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. Let $D_N,D_S$ be the closed northern and southern hemispheres. Specify smooth lifts $u_\alpha:U_\alpha\to SU(2)$ on open neighborhoods $U_\alpha\supset D_\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}T_3=n_\infty$. On their common equator $C$, oriented as $\partial D_N$, the transition is $u_S=u_Nh$, where $h(\varphi)=\exp(\theta(\varphi)T_3)$, $\varphi\in[0,2\pi]$ runs positively around $C$, and $\theta:[0,2\pi]\to\mathbb R$ is a specified smooth lift.

For $R>0$, put $\iota_R(\omega)=R\omega$ and $F=\tfrac12F_{ij}dx^i\wedge dx^j$. Define the adapted angular forms

$$\mathcal A_{\alpha,R}=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha^{-1}}(\iota_R^*A)+u_\alpha^{-1}du_\alpha,\qquad \mathcal F_{\alpha,R}=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha^{-1}}(\iota_R^*F).$$

Require pointwise convergence $\mathcal A_{\alpha,R}\to\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}$ on $D_\alpha$, with $\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}$ extending as a $C^1$ one-form to $U_\alpha$. Require its curvature $\mathcal F_{\alpha,\infty}:=d\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}+\tfrac12[\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}\wedge\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}]$ to extend as a $C^1$ two-form to $U_\alpha$, and $\mathcal F_{\alpha,R}\to\mathcal F_{\alpha,\infty}$ uniformly on $D_\alpha$. Norms and convergence use the round metric of the unit sphere and $\kappa$. Define the limiting tangential covariant derivative by its local expression

$$D_{\mathrm{tan}}n_\infty|_{D_\alpha}:=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}\bigl(dT_3+[\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty},T_3]\bigr)=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}[\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty},T_3],$$

where $dT_3=0$ and the bracket is evaluated on tangent vectors. The transition law makes these expressions agree on the equator. Require $D_{\mathrm{tan}}n_\infty=0$. Let $d\Omega$ be the outward round area form on $S^2$ and define $B_\infty:S^2\to\mathfrak{su}(2)$ by

$$\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}\mathcal F_{\alpha,\infty}=B_\infty\,d\Omega\quad\hbox{on }D_\alpha.$$

Curvature covariance makes this definition agree on $C$. Equivalently, $B_\infty(\omega)=\lim_{R\to\infty}R^2\sum_i\omega_iB_i(R\omega)$ uniformly on each hemisphere, since $\iota_R^*F=R^2\sum_i\omega_iB_i(R\omega)\,d\Omega$. It is the scaled radial magnetic field, not the unscaled spatial field. Require $[B_\infty(\omega),n_\infty(\omega)]=0$, meaning that its value belongs to the pointwise stabilizer Lie algebra $\{X\in\mathfrak{su}(2):[X,n_\infty(\omega)]=0\}$. These convergence and reduction conditions are adopted boundary hypotheses, not consequences asserted for every finite-energy field. The surface limit below is also required to exist.

The admissible external Wilson probes include the fundamental doublet, on which $T_3$ has weights $\pm\tfrac12$; this specifies the electric probe lattice without adding a propagating fundamental matter field. Define the classical magnetic surface charge and its energy normalization by

$$m:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\,\hat x_i\,dS,\qquad T:=g^{-2}m,$$

where $\hat x=x/|x|$ is the outward unit normal and $dS$ is Euclidean area. The transition increment $\theta(2\pi)-\theta(0)$ is not assumed to be quantized in this definition. These are adopted classical model data; they assert no empirical law, quantum continuum construction, supersymmetry representation, or quantum BPS state.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On oriented Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ with $\epsilon_{123}=1$, use the zero-potential static model with global group $SU(2)$, $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, $F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j]$, $D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi]$, and $B_i=\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$. Let $g>0$ be dimensionless, $v>0$ of dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, and $A_i,\Phi$ be smooth static fields. Assume $|\Phi|_\kappa\to v$, $\Phi(R\,\cdot)/v\to n_\infty$ in $C^\infty(S^2,\mathfrak{su}(2))$, and the boundary reduction specified below. Let $D_N,D_S\subset S^2$ be the closed northern and southern hemispheres, and choose smooth lifts $u_\alpha$ on neighborhoods of $D_\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}T_3=n_\infty$ and transition $u_S=u_Nh$ on their common equator, where $h(\varphi)=\exp(\theta(\varphi)T_3)$ and $\theta:[0,2\pi]\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth lift. For $\iota_R:S^2\to S_R^2$, $\iota_R(\omega)=R\omega$, define on each $D_\alpha$ the fixed-frame angular connection, curvature, and normalized Higgs field by

$$\mathcal A_{\alpha,R}:=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha^{-1}}(\iota_R^*A)+u_\alpha^{-1}du_\alpha,\qquad \mathcal F_{\alpha,R}:=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha^{-1}}(\iota_R^*F),\qquad q_{\alpha,R}:=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha^{-1}}\bigl(\Phi(R\,\cdot)/v\bigr).$$

Assume that $\mathcal A_{\alpha,R}$ converges pointwise on each closed hemisphere to $\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}$, which extends as a $C^1$ one-form to a neighborhood of $D_\alpha$. Define its curvature by $\mathcal F_{\alpha,\infty}:=d\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}+\tfrac12[\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}\wedge\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}]$, and assume it extends as a $C^1$ two-form to a neighborhood of $D_\alpha$. Also assume $\mathcal F_{\alpha,R}\to\mathcal F_{\alpha,\infty}$ uniformly on each closed hemisphere. The fixed-frame right-action transition gives $\mathcal A_{S,\infty}=\operatorname{Ad}_{h^{-1}}\mathcal A_{N,\infty}+h^{-1}dh$. The smooth Higgs-field limit gives $q_{\alpha,R}\to T_3$ uniformly. Define $D_{\mathrm{tan}}n_\infty|_{D_\alpha}:=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}[\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty},T_3]$ and require it to vanish. Define $B_\infty:S^2\to\mathfrak{su}(2)$ by $\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}\mathcal F_{\alpha,\infty}=B_\infty\,d\Omega$ on $D_\alpha$, with $d\Omega$ the outward unit-sphere area form. Curvature covariance identifies the two definitions on the equator. Equivalently $B_\infty(\omega)=\lim_{R\to\infty}R^2\sum_i\omega_iB_i(R\omega)$ uniformly on each hemisphere. Require $[B_\infty(\omega),n_\infty(\omega)]=0$, which is the stated stabilizer-algebra condition. The equator is oriented as the boundary of $D_N$, and the admissible external electric probes include the fundamental doublet. If the surface flux limit

$$m=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\hat x_i\,dS$$

exists, define

$$\nu:=-\frac{\theta(2\pi)-\theta(0)}{4\pi}.$$

Then $\nu\in\mathbb Z$ and the classical magnetic surface charge and energy-normalized surface term are

$$m=4\pi v\nu,\qquad T=\frac{m}{g^2}=\frac{4\pi v}{g^2}\nu.$$

This is flux quantization for the stated global form, boundary reduction, and probe lattice; it does not assert a universal normalization for other groups or global forms.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use natural units on Minkowski $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and oriented Euclidean spatial slice with $\epsilon_{123}=1$. Fix the global group $SU(2)$, basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, and positive $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. Let $g>0$ be dimensionless and let $A_i,\Phi$ be smooth static fields in the zero-potential adjoint-Higgs model, with $[A_i]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j]$, $D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi]$, and $B_i=\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$. Require the model's smooth finite-energy boundary reduction: $|\Phi|_\kappa\to v>0$ for a fixed $v$ of dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, with $n_\infty(\omega)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\Phi(R\omega)/v$ in $C^\infty(S^2,\mathfrak{su}(2))$. Use the adapted limiting connections $\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty}$ of the static-sector Definition: the tangential condition is $[\mathcal A_{\alpha,\infty},T_3]=0$ in each adapted frame. The scaled radial limit $B_\infty(\omega):=\lim_{R\to\infty}R^2\sum_i\omega_iB_i(R\omega)$ exists uniformly on each closed hemisphere and satisfies $[B_\infty(\omega),n_\infty(\omega)]=0$. Suppose the energy

$$E=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x$$

is finite and the model's asymptotic reduction and surface limit

$$m=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\hat x_i\,dS$$

exist. Put $T=m/g^2$. Then both identities hold:

$$E=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\kappa(B_i-D_i\Phi,B_i-D_i\Phi)\,d^3x+T,$$

$$E=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\kappa(B_i+D_i\Phi,B_i+D_i\Phi)\,d^3x-T.$$

Consequently $E\ge |T|$. If $T>0$, equality holds exactly when $B_i=D_i\Phi$ for every $i$ and every $x$; if $T<0$, equality holds exactly when $B_i=-D_i\Phi$ everywhere. If $T=0$, equality holds exactly when $B_i=0$ and $D_i\Phi=0$ everywhere. These are conditional classical deductions for the adopted energy functional; the word BPS here refers only to classical energy saturation and asserts no quantum state or supersymmetry central-charge relation.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use natural units on oriented Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ with $\epsilon_{123}=1$, the zero-potential static model with one real adjoint Higgs field, no other dynamical matter, and global group $SU(2)$ (not $SO(3)$). Let $A_i,\Phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3,\mathfrak{su}(2))$ have dimensions $[A_i]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$. Let $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $g>0$ be dimensionless, and $v>0$ have dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$. The fields use $F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j]$, $D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi]$, $B_i=\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, and $E=(2g^2)^{-1}\int\sum_i\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x$. The allowed external electric probes include the fundamental doublet. For $x\in\mathbb R^3$ with $r=|x|>0$, $n_i=x_i/r$, and $u=vr$, define

$$H(u)=\coth u-\frac1u,\qquad K(u)=\frac{u}{\sinh u},\qquad \Phi^a(x)=-vH(u)n_a,\qquad A_i^a(x)=\epsilon_{aij}n_j\frac{1-K(u)}r.$$

Use the removable analytic limits $H(0)=0$ and $K(0)=1$. At infinity $\Phi\to-v\,\hat x^aT_a$, the unbroken algebra is its pointwise stabilizer, and the equatorial transition $h(\varphi)=\exp(\theta(\varphi)T_3)$ has integer $\nu=-(\theta(2\pi)-\theta(0))/(4\pi)$ in the fundamental-doublet-compatible SU(2) convention. In these conventions the fields extend smoothly to $r=0$, satisfy the positive-charge Bogomolny equation $B_i=D_i\Phi$, have $m=4\pi v$ and $\nu=1$, and have finite energy $E=4\pi v/g^2$. They give an explicit smooth unit-flux solution of the first-order classical Bogomolny equation that saturates the classical energy bound. No quantum state, supersymmetry representation, or empirical observation is asserted.
